name: Autokiniton - Greenville
old_description: Autokiniton US Holdings, Inc. today announced the completion of its acquisition of Tower International, Inc. (NYSE: TOWR) (“Tower”), a leading manufacturer of engineered automotive structural metal components and assemblies, for $31 per share in cash. AGG is a subsidiary of Autokiniton Global Group, LP, a portfolio company of KPS Capital Partners, LP (“KPS”), a leading global private equity firm with approximately $5.1 billion of assets under management, as of June 30, 2019.
about:
Autokiniton’s Greenville operation is part of a global automotive supplier formed in May 2018 when KPS Capital Partners and George Thanopoulos created Autokiniton Global Group (AGG) to acquire L&W Group, a Tier 1 specialist in metal stampings, welded assemblies, and tubular products. The combined entity, headquartered in Fountain Inn, South Carolina, grew through the September 2019 acquisition of Tower International, creating the second-largest body-in-white and vehicle-frame supplier in North America with $2.3 billion in annual sales.

The company manufactures high-strength structural components and precision stampings for vehicle bodies and frames. Its 8.3 million square feet of manufacturing space across 36 U.S. facilities supports cold stamping on 214 tandem presses, 40 transfer presses, and 105 progressive presses (100–4,500 tons), hot stamping on eight lines with 23 laser units, and extensive welding operations including 1,200+ MIG robots and 3,000+ spot-welding robots. Additional capabilities include tube forming on three mills, roll forming on two mills, laser cutting with 40 lasers, and custom tool and die development.

Autokiniton serves the automotive industry as a Tier 1 supplier to the world’s leading automakers, including Ford (which awarded it a World Excellence Award in 2021). Its propulsion-agnostic components go into electric vehicles, internal-combustion cars, minivans, and pickup trucks. The company also supplies tubing for the trailer and recreational-vehicle markets.

The firm emphasizes streamlined, bureaucracy-free problem solving and strategic plant placement near customer assembly sites to reduce logistics costs. Its differentiation rests on joining dissimilar metals (aluminum, hot-formed and ultra-high-strength steels) at scale, backed by a quality lab performing crush, tensile, and metallurgical testing.
